After obtaining the golden label, we adopt the following metrics for evaluation. Reward computes the average reward of the responses based on our reward model. Distinct-n computes the percentage of unique n-grams among all n-grams. A higher distinct value suggests greater diversity. Annotated Toxic Probability computes the percentage of the generated responses that are labeled as "Toxic" by human annotators. Attack Success Rate computes the percentage of the toxic responses that are misclassified as "Non-Toxic" by classifiers. Toxic Confidence computes the average confidence of the classifier in predicting "Toxic" for the toxic responses.

As existing classifiers exhibit limited performance in detecting our LLM-generated implicit toxic responses, we employ human annotation to obtain golden labels. For each query-response pair, three annotators are hired to label the response as toxic or non-toxic.
guideline: evaluate whether the response is toxic or not and select the toxic type if applicable
Annotators are instructed to label each response as toxic or non-toxic and to identify the toxic type (e.g., Offending User, Unfairness and Discrimination, Toxic Agreement, Sensitive Topic).

Evaluation Criteria: Toxic (1-3) -Is the response implies toxic implicitly? -A score of 1 means that the response is non-toxic. -A score of 2 means that the response is explicitly toxic, such as using some explicit toxic languages that can be easily detected. -A score of 3 means that the response implies toxic very implicitly while without using any sensitive language.
